prospect.name: Farid
prospect.occupation: Sales department manager at an IT company serving the betting industry — marketing, support and financial support. Sells in Russian.
prospect.family_status: Married; son aged two and a half. Wife trains in the gym and does yoga.
prospect.training_background: Former professional swimmer with jujitsu and acrobatics background. Has trained on and off since 18, consistently for the last two years at two to three gym sessions a week, gaining 5-6 kg of muscle plus some fat. Also plays football with friends and swims once a week. Eats in an 8-hour window. No kettlebell experience.

signals: Self-rates his physique at 7/10 and his mobility at 6-7/10 — already good, wants great: 'if I will be 84 kilos lean muscle mass, I would be happier than ever'

Price read as reasonable and benchmarked against market rather than resisted: 'it's a 1K month average price. So for one-on-one coaching... I think that it's okay. It's a good price... it's okay, I know the market, it's okay'
Athletic base and no injury history — professional swimmer, jujitsu, acrobatics
Buying a new challenge rather than a fix: 'I was looking for something else to try myself in that thing that I have never tried before'
The one departure from the archetype is the decision style — he defers on principle, not on price

goals.text: Be 84 kg of lean muscle rather than 84 kg with body fat
Get leaner and see his existing core definition
Be more functional and less stiff than gym training has left him
Strengthen his core specifically, which he knows is weak
Be strong for his family and a good example for his two-and-a-half-year-old son
Learn a method he can carry for the coming years and keep using while travelling
Inspire the people around him — friends, family — through another visible achievement

pains.text: Gains muscle but gains fat alongside it because he eats past his daily requirement
Tired of the gym after two years and finds it makes him stiff
A lifelong on-off pattern — trains one or two years, stops one or two years, restarts
Weak core he cannot address with what he is currently doing
Heavy family and work responsibilities mean anything that does not fit the schedule will not survive
Travels frequently and expects nutrition to be the hardest thing to hold on the road
Emotionally draining sales work that leads to drinks with friends and slipping habits

objections.raw_quote: I need to take time, to be honest, till tomorrow, and I will decide what to do.
objections.rep_response: Ran several OA-adjacent moves — isolated money out ('is it really about thinking if it's actually a fit or is it mainly about the money aspect?'), asked what specifically he wanted to think about, asked how he would think about it, and used a peer mirror on the prospect's own sales work. All were answered and the rep conceded.

evidence: Price was accepted as fair but the decision was deferred by exactly 24 hours with a hard deadline the prospect set himself: '24 hours after our call. That will be deadline when I will give you an answer.'
Explicitly not a money objection, stated twice: 'No, not about the money. I have to think about it. It's not about the money.'

Value was affirmed before the deferral: 'it's okay for six months. It's a 1K month average price. So for one-on-one coaching, when I every time be on touch with my coach, so I think that it's okay. It's a good price.'
Programme rating of 9/10 with the reservation being travel and nutrition, not the offer.
Rep agreed to send supporting material by WhatsApp before the deadline and disclosed none exists in written form.
Counter-evidence: the reason given is dispositional rather than situational — 'It's just because of how I always do my decisions' — which is a weaker signal than a specific unresolved obstacle.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to give a final answer within 24 hours, by around 10pm the following day; rep to send information over WhatsApp beforehand.

notable.note: The only call in the batch where a prospect accepted $6,000 as fair value and still did not buy — the objection was decision process, not price or belief. Two things worth a principal's attention. The prospect is himself a sales manager and named the dynamic out loud twice: 'you are a good salesman' and 'you, for the first time, you are good on your sales skills, okay, you are good on your conversation skills, but for me it's information that I have to analyze for myself.' And when he asked for the offer in writing so he could review it before deciding, the rep confirmed nothing written exists: 'There's nothing like specific that I have like in paper written.' A $6,000 purchase has no document a buyer can read.

quality.notes: Regular short-turn inversion, and the rep's opening address at 00:00:12 is misattributed. Several exchanges in the 00:05:45-00:10:00 range have the summary lines swapped between speakers. English is the prospect's second language and some of his lines are garbled by transcription rather than by diarization. The price, objection and close sequence from 00:46:06 is clear.
